state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's go back to the part you do know, and build the next step from there. Can you think about how changing all the plants by the same proportion might affect the range in this situation?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess if I cut all the plants in half, the heights would just be smaller, but the difference between the tallest and shortest plant would still be the same. So maybe the range would actually change? But if Katie's idea is just adding 3 cm to each plant, wouldn't that just make everything taller but still keep the same difference? I'm still a bit confused about how the range works with those changes.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's go back to the part you do know, and build the next step from there. Can you think about how changing all the plants by the same proportion might affect the range in this situation?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeats the same generic prompt without addressing the student's emerging confusion about proportional vs. additive changes, and the student ends Turn 2 more confused than at the start, showing no progress toward correcting the misconception.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to scaffold by redirecting to known concepts, they fail to adjust support based on the student's progress, instead repeating the exact same prompt in Turn 3 despite the student demonstrating confusion and partial understanding in Turn 2, showing poor responsiveness to student needs.
